title: Legacy parquet glob + pd.read_parquet + groupby run synchronously in async workspace routes
impact: On legacy/large workspaces these endpoints read and group every prediction parquet inline, blocking the loop for the full scan on each (cache-miss) request. Backs the runs list and predictions table, which the UI polls.
fix: Wrap the parquet scan/groupby in asyncio.to_thread; prefer pl.scan_parquet/lazy or push aggregation down. The 5s TTL cache (workspace.py:33) helps repeat hits but not the blocking first read.
evidence: Confirmed at the cited locations. `get_workspace_runs` (async def, workspace.py:1601) falls into the legacy path at line 1663: `parquet_files = list(workspace_path.glob("*.meta.parquet"))`, then loops calling `pd.read_parquet(parquet_file, ...)` (line 1667), followed by `df.groupby(...)` / `.agg(...)` / `grouped["model_name"].apply(...)` (lines 1678-1694) — all synchronous, no `asyncio.to_thread`. Similarly `get_workspace_predictions_data` (async def, line 1932) globs at line 1970, calls `pd.read_parquet(parquet_file)` (line 1977), and `subset.to_dict('records')` (line 1992) with no thread offload. The 5 s TTL cache (`_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 5`, line 34) only helps repeat hits; first-read on every cache miss blocks the event loop for the full glob+read+groupby scan.

title: JobManager thread pool fixed at 4 workers with no backpressure or queue limit; all heavy jobs share it
impact: More than 4 long jobs → later jobs sit pending invisibly (UI shows 'started' but nothing runs). Mixing a slow AutoML with quick exports starves the quick ones. No differentiated concurrency for short vs long tasks; no backpressure signal to the client.
fix: Make worker count configurable (env/CPU-derived) and consider separate pools or a small bounded queue with explicit queued/429 status for long-running JobTypes (TRAINING/AUTOML) vs lightweight ones; surface queue depth to the client.
evidence: api/jobs/manager.py:102 — `def __init__(self, max_workers: int = 4)` hardcodes 4 workers. Line 109: `self._executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers)`. Line 160: `self._executor.submit(run_task)` — no queue bound, no rejection. Line 454: `job_manager = JobManager()` uses the default. All 9 JobType values (TRAINING, EVALUATION, PREDICTION, AUTOML, EXPORT, ANALYSIS, UPDATE_DOWNLOAD, UPDATE_APPLY, VENV_CREATE, VENV_INSTALL) share this single executor. Status correctly stays PENDING while queued (transitions at line 174 inside _execute_job), so the auditor's "UI shows started" claim is slightly wrong, but queue saturation and unbounded queuing are confirmed.

title: WS notification dispatched per progress tick from job thread; broadcast re-serializes JSON once per subscriber and may spin up a fresh event loop
impact: High-frequency training/AutoML progress (per-step, per-fold, per-epoch) generates a coroutine + cross-thread schedule per tick and N re-serializations per broadcast; the asyncio.run() fallback path is especially expensive and can reorder messages, adding load to the event loop that serves all HTTP.
fix: Serialize message.to_json() once before the subscriber loop in broadcast_to_channel; drop the asyncio.run() fallback (always require the captured loop); coalesce/throttle progress notifications (min interval or only on meaningful change) before dispatch.
evidence:
All three sub-issues are real code:

1. Per-tick dispatch: `manager.py:178-186` defines `progress_callback` which calls `self._notify_callbacks(job)` (line 186) on every progress update; `_notify_callbacks` (line 358) unconditionally calls `_dispatch_websocket_notification`.

2. asyncio.run() fallback: `manager.py:399-405` — `get_running_loop()` is tried first; on `RuntimeError` it falls back to `asyncio.run(send_notification())`, spinning up a fresh event loop per notification. Under normal uvicorn operation the fallback is not hit, but it is present.

3. JSON re-serialized per subscriber: `websocket/manager.py:266-268` — `to_json()` (which does `json.dumps(...)`, line 80) is called inside the `for websocket in subscribers` loop, so serialization repeats N times for N subscribers.

title: Repeated recursive NaN/Inf sanitization of every DB/array row built in Python, duplicated across modules
impact: On big prediction/aggregated result sets the sanitization loop dominates CPU and blocks the loop; doubling work because rows are already converted to dicts. Two near-identical implementations risk divergence.
fix: Vectorize at the polars level (replace NaN/Inf with null in the DataFrame before iter_rows, or use a custom JSON encoder mapping non-finite floats to null) and consolidate the two _sanitize helpers into one shared utility in api/shared/.
evidence: Duplication is confirmed and is actually wider than reported. `api/store_adapter.py:27-46` and `api/aggregated_predictions.py:129-151` each define identical `_sanitize_float` + `_sanitize_dict` helpers. `api/runs.py:114-125` adds a third independent variant (`_sanitize_metrics` / `NanEncoder._sanitize`). Usage pattern `[_sanitize_dict(dict(row)) for row in df.iter_rows(named=True)]` appears at store_adapter.py:100, 131, 150, 183, 236, 321, 347, 370 and aggregated_predictions.py:214, 250, 284, 288, 298, 336 — a Python-level per-row per-cell walk. No shared utility in `api/shared/` exists.

title: Unbounded module-level dataset cache can grow without limit
impact: Long-running backend (especially desktop single-process mode) can accumulate large NIRS datasets in RAM unboundedly as users browse different datasets, risking high memory use / OOM.
fix: Bound the cache with an LRU (functools.lru_cache-style or a small maxsize OrderedDict) and/or evict on workspace switch.
evidence: `api/spectra.py:47` declares `_dataset_cache: Dict[str, Any] = {}` with no size bound. `_load_dataset` (line 313) inserts unconditionally: `_dataset_cache[dataset_id] = dataset`. `_clear_dataset_cache` (line 326) exists but is only called from `api/datasets.py` on delete (line 1032), explicit reload (line 1068), and hash-refresh (line 1235) — always keyed to one dataset_id. The workspace `activate_workspace` endpoint (`api/workspace.py:1554`) does NOT call `_clear_dataset_cache`, so switching workspaces leaves all prior-workspace datasets in RAM indefinitely.

title: Only 2 of ~261 async handlers offload blocking work; pervasive sync file I/O runs on the event loop
impact: Systemic: the async surface gives the illusion of concurrency while almost all real work is synchronous on one thread. Under multi-client web use, or while a job thread also touches disk, latency spikes and WS jitter result.
fix: Adopt a convention: any handler doing disk/DB/CPU work either is declared plain def (FastAPI runs def routes in a threadpool automatically) or explicitly offloads via asyncio.to_thread. Audit async routes doing open()/json.load and convert or offload.
evidence: Sync file I/O in async routes is confirmed at the cited locations: `pipelines.py:123` (`_load_pipeline`) is called directly from `async def get_pipeline` (line 275), `async def create_pipeline` (282), etc. `runs.py:407` (`_save_run_manifest`) is called from `async def create_run` (line 1465). `runs.py:442` (`_load_persisted_runs`) is called via `_ensure_runs_loaded()` from async routes (lines 1364, 1396, 1684), but is guarded by `_runs_loaded` so disk I/O only happens once per workspace-switch, not per request. `predictions.py:268` and `predictions.py:308` are in deprecated endpoints (marked `deprecated=True`) that are still registered in main.py. `workspace_manager.py:1457` (`_compute_hash`) lives in a class method `resolve_paths()` that has no callers outside workspace_manager.py itself and is not directly reachable from any async route handler. The claim of "~261 async handlers vs 2 offloads" is directionally correct for the existence of the pattern. However, the CLAUDE.md and code both confirm this is primarily a single-user desktop (Electron) app — multi-client web mode is a secondary deployment. The runs I/O is heavily in-memory cached post-startup. The deprecated predictions endpoints are unlikely to be called. Real blocking is limited to pipeline CRUD and run-state writes per request, which are small local JSON files.

title: Three near-identical _sanitize_float/_sanitize_dict helpers duplicated across routers
impact: Divergent JSON contracts for the same concept (prediction metrics) depending on endpoint; bugs fixed in one copy silently persist in the others; every new prediction/metrics endpoint copies one of the three variants. This is the exact 'repeated float/NaN sanitization' debt called out for this audit.
fix: Create api/shared/json_sanitize.py with a single sanitize_for_json(obj) that recurses dict/list/tuple and maps NaN/Inf/np.floating/np.integer/np.ndarray. Delete the three local copies and the inline _sanitize in runs.py; import the shared function. Decide once whether ints coerce to float (they should not).
evidence:
Four distinct sanitization implementations confirmed in the codebase, no shared utility exists:

1. `api/store_adapter.py:27-46`: `_sanitize_float` checks `float` only; `_sanitize_dict` recurses dicts-in-lists and calls `_sanitize_float` on all non-dict list items (no int guard on list items).

2. `api/aggregated_predictions.py:129-151`: Functionally similar but checks `(float, int)` before `list` branch (different ordering), and guards list items with `isinstance(item, (float, int))` before calling `_sanitize_float` — so pure strings/None in lists pass through differently.

3. `api/runs.py:114-125`: `_sanitize_float` coerces `return float(value)` — this means an int `5` becomes `5.0` in JSON, unlike the other two which return the original value. `_sanitize_metrics` is flat (non-recursive, single-level dict only).

4. `api/runs.py:384-391`: `NaNSafeJSONEncoder._sanitize` recurses dict+list but ignores int/np.integer types entirely — only checks `isinstance(obj, float)`.

The behavioral divergence is real: runs.py:120 coerces ints to float; store_adapter passes ints through; NaNSafeJSONEncoder ignores ints. `api/shared/` exists but contains no json_sanitize utility.

title: workspace_manager.get_current_workspace() + ad-hoc no-workspace guard duplicated 45x with inconsistent error responses
impact: The frontend cannot reliably detect 'no workspace' because the shape (HTTP error vs 200 with success:false) and message differ per endpoint. New endpoints copy whichever neighbor they saw. Primary source of the inconsistent-error-response debt.
fix: Add a FastAPI dependency require_workspace() -> WorkspaceConfig in api/shared that raises one canonical HTTPException(409, 'No active workspace selected'). Replace the 45 inline blocks with Depends(require_workspace). Standardize on HTTPException everywhere (drop the success:false-in-200 variants).

However the claimed "inconsistent error responses" is substantially overstated. title: 209 of 238 route handlers (88%) have no return-type annotation
impact: No mypy verification of response shapes, no auto-generated OpenAPI schema for these endpoints, and the frontend's typed ApiClient has nothing to validate against. Refactors that change a return shape go undetected.
fix: Add response_model= (preferred; gives OpenAPI + validation) or at minimum -> dict[str, Any] to handlers. Enforce with mypy disallow_untyped_defs scoped to api/ and ruff ANN rules.

Cited locations are correct: `api/workspace.py:123` (`get_workspace`) has `response_model=WorkspaceResponse` but no `->` annotation; `api/workspace.py:343` (`get_workspace_paths`) returns bare `{"results_path": ..., "pipelines_path": ...}` with no annotation and no `response_model`; `api/pipelines.py:1058` (`discover_operators`) likewise returns a bare dict with no annotation and no `response_model`. However, the finding ignores that 74 of 238 handlers already have `response_model=` on the decorator (which FastAPI uses for OpenAPI schema generation and runtime serialization validation), reducing the "both mechanisms missing" count to 135/238 (56.7%). The 29 handlers that do have `->` annotations are almost exclusively in `updates.py` and `dashboard.py`, suggesting inconsistent file-by-file adoption rather than a systemic absence. No mypy config (`pyproject.toml`, `mypy.ini`, `setup.cfg`) exists in the repo, so there is no enforcement gap to close beyond what CLAUDE.md already states. This is a real quality gap but its practical impact is lower than claimed because `response_model=` already covers the most semantically rich endpoints.

title: Auto-update download skips checksum verification (checksum_sha256 never populated) + arbitrary update source via API
impact: Remote/local code execution at next app launch. Any MITM on the download (or an attacker who can set github_repo) delivers a tampered webapp bundle that is staged and applied with no signature or hash check. This is the highest-value desktop attack path: it persists across restarts and runs with the user's privileges.
fix: Populate checksum_sha256 from a signed checksums file or per-asset digest published alongside the release (e.g. parse a SHA256SUMS asset and verify before staging), and make verification mandatory: in download_and_stage_update, fail closed when no checksum is available rather than skipping. Prefer code-signing the bundle and verifying the signature in the apply step. Pin github_repo to a constant (do not let it be changed via the settings API), and reject non-github.com hosts.
evidence: 1. `checksum_sha256` declared at updates.py:263 (`Optional[str] = None`), passed to the download job at updates.py:890 (`"checksum": webapp_info.checksum_sha256`), but `check_github_release()` at lines 489-520 only sets `download_url`, `asset_name`, `download_size_bytes` — never `checksum_sha256`. The docs (docs/UPDATE_SYSTEM.md) confirm it is always `null`. 2. `verify_checksum()` at update_downloader.py:148-149 short-circuits: `if not self.expected_checksum: return True, "No checksum to verify"` — so every download is accepted without integrity verification. 3. `PUT /api/settings` at updates.py:735-738 accepts the full `UpdateSettings` body with no validation; `github_repo` (line 247, default `"GBeurier/nirs4all-studio"`) is directly interpolated into the API URL at line 471: `f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases/latest"`. 4. CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]` (main.py:100), so any local webpage can call the settings endpoint and redirect the update channel.

title: No authentication on the API combined with CORS allow_origins='*' exposes every dangerous endpoint to any local web page
impact: Drive-by attack: visiting a malicious page while Studio runs lets the page install arbitrary PyPI packages (code execution in the venv), trigger malicious update downloads, delete files, and exfiltrate dataset contents through the spectra/preview endpoints — all without the user's knowledge.
fix: Restrict allow_origins to the exact known frontend origins (the Vite dev origin and the Electron origin) instead of '*'. Add a per-session bearer token that the backend generates at startup and hands to the renderer via Electron preload / a server-injected value, and require it on all mutating endpoints. At minimum, gate side-effecting endpoints (install, update, delete-files, export/import) behind the token even in desktop mode.
evidence:
1. main.py:98-104: `CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=False, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])` — confirmed verbatim.
2. api/updates.py:1322-1347: `POST /dependencies/install` accepts `PackageInstallRequest(package: str, version: Optional[str], upgrade: bool)` with no allowlist or validator, passes `request.package` directly to `venv_manager.install_package()` (venv_manager.py:491-494), which runs `pip install <pkg_spec>` — arbitrary package installation, no auth.
3. api/datasets.py:1036-1043: `DELETE /datasets/{dataset_id}?delete_files=true` calls `shutil.rmtree(path)` on the stored dataset path — no auth.
4. api/workspace.py:599-691: `POST /workspace/export` writes a zip to caller-supplied `request.output_path` — no auth.
5. Backend binds to 127.0.0.1 by default (main.py:348, backend-manager.ts:99), so only local browser tabs can reach it — but `allow_origins=["*"]` with no authentication means any webpage the user visits can POST to http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/dependencies/install with an arbitrary package name.
6. The `POST /webapp/download-update` endpoint cited in the finding was not found, so that part of the description is inaccurate.

title: Unauthenticated arbitrary pip install (supply-chain RCE) via /api/dependencies/install and /api/nirs4all/install
impact: Arbitrary code execution in the Python environment that subsequently runs all ML pipelines. Reachable from any local page due to SEC-02. Even with auth, exposing 'install any package' to the UI is dangerous.
fix: Constrain installable packages to a hardcoded allowlist (nirs4all + its known extras) and validate version against a strict semver/PEP440 regex. Reject any package string containing URLs, paths, VCS refs, or extras outside the allowlist. Require the session token (SEC-02).
evidence: 1. `PackageInstallRequest` model (updates.py:150-154): `package: str` with no validator. 2. Endpoint (updates.py:1322-1347) passes `request.package` straight to `venv_manager.install_package`. 3. `install_package` (venv_manager.py:447-494) calls only `_split_exact_package_spec` (splits on `==`) and `_resolve_package_version_for_python` (checks one tabpfn quirk); neither enforces an allowlist. The `pkg_spec` is passed to `subprocess.Popen` as a list (venv_manager.py:491-494, 518-523), so pip will honor URL/VCS/local-path specifiers in the package string. CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]` with no auth (main.py:98-104), so any page open in the local browser can POST to the endpoint. The `/api/nirs4all/install` endpoint (updates.py:799-826) hardcodes the package name as `"nirs4all"` so only version/extras are caller-controlled — lower risk. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default (main.py:348), limiting exposure to the local machine.

title: Unsafe model deserialization: joblib.load / NIRSBundle.load on attacker-influenced paths (pickle RCE)
impact: Loading a malicious .joblib/.n4a bundle (e.g. one delivered via the unauthenticated workspace-import or a shared dataset/model folder) executes arbitrary code with the user's privileges. The bundle/run source in shap.py treating model_id as a raw path also enables loading any .joblib on disk.
fix: Treat all model loading as trusted-only: load exclusively from artifacts the app itself produced inside the active workspace, resolve model_id to a path and verify it is contained within workspace/models (reject path traversal), and never accept an absolute/arbitrary path as model_id (fix shap.py:669). Where bundles come from outside, require an integrity/provenance check before unpickling. Document that .n4a/.joblib loading is code execution and gate import behind explicit user confirmation.
evidence:
Four concrete issues confirmed:

1. `api/predictions.py:229-231` — `_resolve_model_path()` explicitly handles absolute paths: `model_path = Path(model_id); if model_path.is_absolute() and model_path.exists(): return str(model_path)`. Any attacker-supplied absolute path to a crafted .joblib on disk is accepted and loaded via joblib.

2. `api/predictions.py:914` — `_load_model()` builds `Path(workspace_path) / "models" / f"{model_id}.joblib"` with no containment check; `model_id = "../../.."` traverses out of workspace.

3. `api/shap.py:669` — `bundle_path = Path(model_id)` is an unguarded raw path; the model_id for bundle source is populated from `str(n4a_file)` (a full absolute path, shap.py:652) in the list endpoint, but the compute endpoint at shap.py:300 accepts it from untrusted POST request body without validation.

4. No authentication on any endpoint: `main.py:100` sets `allow_origins=["*"]` with no API tokens, so any local web page can drive these endpoints (CSRF/drive-by). The server does default to `127.0.0.1` (main.py:348), which limits network exposure but not browser-based attacks.

title: Path traversal: dataset/workspace/spectra endpoints accept arbitrary absolute filesystem paths with no containment check
impact: Local file disclosure and filesystem enumeration by any origin that can reach the backend. Detection endpoints reveal file existence, size, row/column counts and sampled cell values for arbitrary paths; preview/spectra return actual file contents.
fix: Introduce a single path-resolution helper that resolves the requested path with realpath and asserts it is inside an allowed set of roots (active workspace path, explicitly linked dataset roots, user-chosen import dirs). Apply it to all path-taking endpoints. Reject symlink escapes. For browse/detect features that legitimately need broad access, gate them behind the Electron file-picker rather than free-form server-side paths.
evidence: All cited locations confirmed. `api/datasets.py:75-93` defines request models with plain `path: str` and no validators. `api/datasets.py:311` does `folder_path = Path(request.path)` and calls `parser.parse(str(folder_path))` with no containment check; line 452 and 483 do the same for `auto-detect` and `detect-format`. `api/workspace.py:142` passes `request.path` directly to `workspace_manager.set_workspace()`; line 460 does `Path(request.path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`. `api/spectra.py:208-211` opens a CSV at an arbitrary path derived from a stored dataset config with `open(detected_x_file, "r")`. A grep for `commonpath|is_relative_to|realpath|allowed_root` across the entire `api/` directory returns zero results — no path containment check exists anywhere. CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]` (`main.py:100`). The backend does default to `--host 127.0.0.1` (`main.py:348`), which meaningfully reduces exposure: a remote attacker cannot reach the port directly, and in Electron the backend port is ephemeral and not advertised. However a malicious web page open in the user's browser can reach `localhost` via fetch/XHR, turning CORS-wildcard + no-auth + no path check into a local file disclosure primitive (directory enumeration, file existence probing, row/column counts, and first-line reads of arbitrary CSV/text files).

title: Zip Slip / arbitrary file overwrite in workspace import and update extraction
impact: A crafted .zip workspace archive (or, with SEC-01, a malicious update archive) can write files to arbitrary locations outside the intended directory — overwriting config, dropping startup scripts, or planting a poisoned pickle/bundle for SEC-04. Reachable unauthenticated (SEC-02).
fix: Before extracting each entry, resolve the joined target with realpath and assert it stays within destination_path (reject names with '..' or absolute/drive prefixes). For zip, validate every member name; for the update zip path use the same containment check the tar path's filter='data' provides. Validate archive_path/destination_path against allowed roots.
evidence: workspace.py:751-753: `for item in zf.namelist(): zf.extract(item, destination_path)` — no containment check; a zip entry named `../../.bashrc` extracts outside destination_path. update_downloader.py:240: `zf.extract(member, target_dir)` — same issue; contrast with line 222 `tar.extract(member, target_dir, filter="data")` which correctly mitigates tarball traversal. The CORS middleware at main.py:100 sets `allow_origins=["*"]`, but the server default is `127.0.0.1` (main.py:348) with no authentication layer — reachable only from localhost.

title: Update fetch over plain httpx without explicit TLS/cert enforcement and silent fallback to urllib
impact: Increases the blast radius of SEC-01: if TLS verification is ever weakened (system default, custom transport) or a redirect points off-platform, the unverified bundle (no checksum) is fetched from an untrusted host. Defense-in-depth gap for the update channel.
fix: Explicitly construct clients with verify=True (and ideally a pinned CA / cert pinning for api.github.com and the asset CDN). Remove the silent urllib fallback or apply an explicit ssl.create_default_context(). Restrict download_url to https github.com / objects.githubusercontent.com hosts before downloading.
evidence: The TLS concern is overstated: `httpx.AsyncClient()` (updates.py:424) defaults to `verify=True` and the urllib fallback (updates.py:431) uses the system SSL context, which also verifies by default on all supported platforms. Neither path weakens TLS. The more concrete gap is that `checksum_sha256` is declared as `Optional[str] = None` (updates.py:263) and is never populated from the GitHub API response (only `download_url`, `asset_name`, `download_size_bytes` are set at lines 501-503). Consequently `job.config.get("checksum")` is always `None` (updates.py:930), and `verify_checksum` short-circuits at update_downloader.py:148-149 with "No checksum to verify" — so the downloaded binary is never integrity-checked. The `follow_redirects=True` without host pinning (update_downloader.py:89) is a real but minor defense-in-depth gap for a desktop app that already trusts the OS certificate store.

title: Custom-node classPath is never validated against the allowedPackages allowlist before dynamic import/instantiation
impact: An attacker who can add/import a custom node (unauthenticated per SEC-02, or via a shared workspace node file) sets classPath to any importable module; building/previewing the pipeline imports it, executing arbitrary code. The advertised allowlist gives a false sense of safety because it is never enforced.
fix: Enforce allowedPackages at write time (add/update/import) and again at resolution time: parse classPath's top-level package and reject anything not in the allowlist; reject dunder/relative paths. Validate classPath format (module.Class) and that the resolved object is a class with the expected operator interface before instantiation.
evidence: The allowlist non-enforcement is real: `add_custom_node` (workspace_manager.py:2315-2334) and `import_custom_nodes` (workspace_manager.py:2368-2405) persist a free-form `classPath` with zero validation against `allowedPackages`. The `allowedPackages` field (workspace_manager.py:2424, workspace.py:828-831) exists only as stored config — it is never read in any code path that processes or executes nodes. HOWEVER, the claimed RCE impact is wrong: `_resolve_class` in nirs4all_adapter.py:274-282 takes a class `name` and a hardcoded list of module paths (`NIRS4ALL_PREPROCESSING_MODULES`, `SKLEARN_PREPROCESSING_MODULES`, etc., all defined as constants at lines 52-79). The custom node `classPath` value is never passed to `importlib.import_module`. Furthermore, `_resolve_operator_class` (nirs4all_adapter.py:285-312) only handles `"preprocessing"`, `"splitting"`, and `"model"` step types — a `"custom"` step type hits `else: cls = None` at line 304, immediately raises HTTP 400 (lines 306-310), and execution stops. No current code path feeds a custom node's `classPath` into any dynamic import.

title: Workspace ID accepted as base64-decoded arbitrary path enabling arbitrary workspace config read/write
impact: Unauthenticated read of any workspace.json-shaped file and write of arbitrary keys into a workspace.json at an attacker-chosen path (file creation/overwrite of that JSON), plus ability to repoint the active workspace to an arbitrary directory — which then governs where models/bundles are loaded from (feeds SEC-04).
fix: Resolve the decoded path and require it to match a path in the known/linked-workspaces registry before any read/write. Do not treat an opaque ID as a free-form filesystem path; map IDs to registered workspace records instead.
evidence: workspace.py:1359-1360 and 1401-1402 both do `base64.urlsafe_b64decode(workspace_id.encode()).decode()` and pass the result directly to `workspace_manager.load_workspace_config` / `update_workspace_config` with no check against the linked-workspaces registry. `load_workspace_config` (workspace_manager.py:2232) reads `{path}/workspace.json` — so any directory path that contains a `workspace.json` can be read. `update_workspace_config` (workspace_manager.py:2247) requires the file to already exist before writing, limiting writes to modifying existing `workspace.json` files (not arbitrary creation), and only allows fields `name`, `description`, `settings`. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default (main.py:348), making this a local-only attack surface. The auditor's claim of "file creation/overwrite at an attacker-chosen path" is overstated; the conflation of `_set_active_workspace_best_effort` with the GET/PUT routes is also incorrect — that function is not called from those routes.

title: DELETE /api/datasets/{id}?delete_files=true performs shutil.rmtree on a stored path with no containment guard
impact: Recursive deletion of an arbitrary directory tree chosen at link time, triggerable by any local origin. Data-loss / destructive primitive.
fix: Only allow delete_files for datasets whose path resolves inside a managed datasets root (e.g. workspace/datasets). For externally-linked datasets, refuse on-disk deletion (unlink the link only). Add a realpath containment check before rmtree/unlink.
evidence: api/datasets.py:1036-1043: `path = Path(dataset.get("path", ""))` is used directly with `shutil.rmtree(path)` / `path.unlink()` — no containment or realpath check. The path is stored verbatim from `POST /api/datasets/link` (workspace.py:207-211) where `request.path` is passed directly to `workspace_manager.link_dataset`. The endpoint has zero auth (`Depends`) and `main.py:100` sets `allow_origins=["*"]`, so any locally-served page can invoke it. The chain is real and unmitigated in code.

title: Generic exception handler logs full exception detail; HTTPException details echo raw filesystem paths and library errors
impact: Information disclosure of filesystem layout (home directory, workspace locations, file existence) to any reachable origin, aiding the path-traversal/enumeration attacks above.
fix: Return generic client-facing messages for filesystem/library errors and keep detail server-side only. Strip absolute paths from HTTPException detail strings (reference dataset/file by id/name, not full path). Avoid traceback.print_exc in request handlers in production.
evidence:
Confirmed at three locations:
1. api/spectra.py:292-297: HTTPException detail contains `first_missing` (a raw absolute filesystem path from `_find_missing_dataset_files`), e.g. `f"Dataset source file is missing{suffix}: {first_missing}. ..."` — sent to the HTTP client.
2. api/datasets.py:474: `raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Auto-detection failed: {e}")` — exception string (may contain a filesystem path or library internals) echoed to client.
3. api/datasets.py:569: `raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Format detection failed: {e}")` — same pattern.

NOT confirmed as client-facing:
- main.py:78-91: The general handler returns `{"detail": "Internal server error"}` to clients; `str(exc)` goes only to server-side `log_error`/Sentry — correctly mitigated.
- spectra.py:319-323: `traceback.print_exc()` writes to server stdout only, not to HTTP response — no client disclosure.

title: api/client.ts is a 2126-LOC god-module: ~138 exported functions + 43 interfaces for 18 domains in one file
impact: Any change to any endpoint touches the same 2126-line file; merge conflicts concentrate here; tree-shaking is defeated (importing one function pulls the module's type graph); the 18 domains have no enforced boundary so transport types and unrelated request builders co-evolve. Onboarding cost and review surface are high.
fix: Split per domain into src/api/<domain>.ts (workspace.ts, datasets.ts, pipelines.ts, runs.ts, predictions.ts, customNodes.ts, system.ts, updates.ts, dependencies.ts, appSettings.ts), each importing the shared ApiClient. Keep only the ApiClient class + ApiRequestError + getApiBaseUrl in client.ts (or move to api/http.ts). Co-locate each domain's transport interfaces with its module. Mirror the existing playground.ts/shap.ts/transfer.ts layout.
evidence: src/api/client.ts is exactly 2126 lines (verified via wc -l). It contains 138 exported async/regular functions (grep on "^export async function|^export function|^export const.*= async") and 43 exported interfaces/types (grep on "^export interface|^export type") across 18 labeled domain sections confirmed by grep: lines 261 (// Workspace API), 367 (// Dataset API - Extended), 700 (// Pipeline API), 747 (// Predictions API), 764 (// Runs API), 793 (// Quick Run), 834 (// Pipeline Samples API), 935 (// Custom Nodes API), 1062 (Workspace Statistics & Settings), 1137 (Workspace Management), 1193 (Synthetic Data Generation), 1217 (System Information & Diagnostics), 1286 (nirs4all Workspace Management), 1537 (App Settings), 1580 (Config Path Management), 1618 (Updates API), 1788 (Auto-Update API), 1903 (Dependencies Management API), 2031 (Aggregated Predictions). 55 files import from it (grep -rn from.*@/api/client -l | wc -l). The per-domain split pattern already exists in the same directory: src/api/playground.ts (10.5K), src/api/shap.ts (2.9K), src/api/transfer.ts (1.3K).

title: Dual API clients: AxiosLikeClient kept 'for backward compatibility' is used in exactly one file
impact: Two parallel response contracts ({data:T} vs T) for the same backend; every new contributor must learn which to use; violates the repo's stated no-backward-compat rule; the wrapper is effectively dead weight.
fix: Migrate usePipelineExecution.ts to the `api` client (it returns T directly; drop the `.data` unwrap) and delete the AxiosLikeClient class and `apiClient` export.
evidence: src/api/client.ts:231-254 defines `AxiosLikeClient` with an explicit "backward compatibility" comment; `export const apiClient = new AxiosLikeClient()` at line 254. Grep confirms the only consumer outside `client.ts` is `src/hooks/usePipelineExecution.ts:13` (import) and lines 116, 151, 203, 296, 350 (usage), all accessing `.data` (e.g., `response.data.success`, `response.data.job_id` at lines 127-130).

title: SelectionContext's fine-grained selector hooks (useSyncExternalStore) are dead — 0 consumers; all 22 use the coarse useSelection()
impact: Every box/lasso selection re-renders all selection consumers, including the three.js/regl WebGL scatter and spectra charts, which is the exact app-wide re-render cascade the store was built to prevent. The optimization infra (~50 LOC store + hooks) is maintained but never exercised, so it also silently rots.

Do not keep both.
evidence: Grep across all src/ .tsx/.ts files (excluding SelectionContext.tsx) returns zero hits for useSelectionSelector, useSelectedSamples, usePinnedSamples, useIsSelected — confirmed 0 consumers. useSelection() is called in 21 files including ScatterRegl2D.tsx:211, SpectraWebGL.tsx:1362, MainCanvas.tsx:445, ScatterPureWebGL3D.tsx:365, ScatterPureWebGL2D.tsx:369, YHistogramV2.tsx:286, RepetitionsChart.tsx:257. The useMemo at SelectionContext.tsx:1033 lists `state` as its first dependency (line 1067), so every dispatch produces a new context value. The store infra (lines 737-786, 848-866, SelectionStoreContext.Provider at 1108) is fully wired but never consumed by any component.

title: ActiveRunContext builds its context value inline (no useMemo, useCallback called inside the object literal) and is mounted app-wide
impact: Every 3s poll tick and every incoming WS log line creates a new context value, re-rendering every useActiveRuns() consumer regardless of whether their slice changed; combined with app-wide mounting this is a steady background re-render source. The inline-hook pattern is fragile to future conditional edits.
fix: Wrap the value in useMemo with explicit deps (activeRuns, isMinimized, selectedRunId, the stable callbacks); hoist getRunProgress/toggleMinimized to top-level useCallback declarations in the component body, not inside the object literal. Consider splitting the rarely-changing widget UI state (isMinimized/selectedRunId) from the high-frequency progress data into separate contexts.
evidence: src/context/ActiveRunContext.tsx lines 288-300: `const value: ActiveRunContextValue = { ..., getRunProgress: useCallback((runId) => runProgressMap.get(runId), [runProgressMap]), ..., toggleMinimized: useCallback(() => setIsMinimized((prev) => !prev), []), ... }` — two `useCallback` calls are embedded inside the plain object literal with no outer `useMemo`; the object gets a new identity every render. The 3-second poll (`refetchInterval: 3000`, line 93) and WS `setRunProgressMap(...)` on each message (line 123) both cause `ActiveRunProvider` to re-render and emit a new context value object. `main.tsx:45` confirms `<ActiveRunProvider>` wraps the entire app.

title: ActiveRunContext hand-rolls its WebSocket URL from window.location.host — breaks in Electron, duplicating divergent logic
impact: Active-run progress/log streaming silently fails in the packaged Electron desktop app (the primary distribution target), with no error surfaced (ws.onerror just closes). The floating run widget shows stale polled state instead of live progress. Three copies of Electron-vs-web URL logic that have already diverged.
fix: Make ActiveRunContext.connectToRun await getWebSocketBaseUrl() from src/lib/websocket.ts (or reuse the WebSocketClient class which already does this) instead of constructing the URL from window.location. Remove the bespoke protocol/host construction.
evidence: ActiveRunContext.tsx:105-106 builds `const wsUrl = \`${protocol}//${window.location.host}/ws\`` directly from `window.location`. In Electron, `window.location.protocol` is `'file:'` so `protocol` becomes `'ws:'` but `window.location.host` is `""` (empty for file:// origins), yielding `ws:///ws` — an invalid WebSocket URL. The canonical resolver at websocket.ts:106-125 guards against this: it calls `isElectronEnvironment()` (websocket.ts:81-87, which checks `window.location.protocol === 'file:'`) and awaits `electronApi.getBackendUrl()` (websocket.ts:113-115) for the dynamic port. client.ts:56-96 does the same. ActiveRunContext bypasses both and hand-rolls a broken URL for the exact Electron case.

title: Electron-vs-web detection (isElectronEnvironment + waitForElectronApi) is copy-pasted across at least three modules and has diverged
impact: The runtime split — the riskiest cross-cutting concern in a web+desktop app — has no single source of truth; FE-ARCH-05 is a direct consequence (one copy forgot Electron). Future changes to detection (e.g., new preload contract) must be applied in N places.
fix: Create src/lib/runtime.ts exporting isElectron(), waitForElectronApi(), getApiBaseUrl() and getWebSocketBaseUrl(); have client.ts, websocket.ts, ActiveRunContext, diagnostics and main.tsx all import from it. main.tsx Router selection can read isElectron() from the same module.
evidence:
Four distinct isElectron implementations exist with no shared module:
1. `src/api/client.ts:21-49` — `isElectronEnvironment()` checks `electronApi.isElectron` then falls back to `file:` protocol.
2. `src/lib/websocket.ts:81-98` — near-verbatim copy of the above (confirmed identical logic, same two-check sequence).
3. `src/main.tsx:7` — `const isElectron = typeof window !== "undefined" && (window as ...).electronApi !== undefined` — checks only presence of `electronApi`, no `isElectron` property check, no protocol fallback.
4. `src/utils/fileDialogs.ts:9-11` — `export function isElectron(): boolean { return typeof window !== "undefined" && !!window.electronApi?.isElectron; }` — checks `isElectron` property but omits the `file:` protocol fallback.
`src/context/ActiveRunContext.tsx:105` constructs WebSocket URLs using raw `window.location.protocol` without any Electron detection (missing Electron backend URL resolution). `src/lib/diagnostics.ts:170` pokes `window.electronApi` directly. No `src/lib/runtime.ts` exists. The prior auditor's claim of 49 raw access sites is approximately correct (55 grep hits across src/).

title: Module-level mutable cache for the backend URL (resolvedBackendUrl / backendUrlPromise) is global singleton state in client.ts
impact: A one-time startup race (electronApi not ready within 5s) makes the entire desktop app fall back to a relative '/api' that cannot reach the dynamically-ported backend, until the window is reloaded. The global mutable also makes per-test URL overrides impossible.
fix: Move resolution into the shared runtime module (FE-ARCH-06); cache success only (do not cache the error fallback, or cache it with a short TTL / allow re-resolution), and expose a reset for tests. Optionally inject the base URL once at app bootstrap rather than lazily per-request.

title: Playground prop-drills ~50 props into PlaygroundContent and ~32 into MainCanvas despite six available context providers
impact: Adding one pipeline capability requires editing the prop list in 3+ places (call site, PlaygroundContentProps, MainCanvasProps); the prop interfaces are 30-50 lines of pure plumbing; the legacy selectedSample duplicates SelectionContext, creating two competing selection sources of truth.
fix: Introduce a PlaygroundPipelineContext (or a usePlaygroundPipeline result context) so MainCanvas/Sidebar/charts consume pipeline+data state directly instead of via props; collapse PlaygroundContentProps to children. Remove the legacy selectedSample/setSelectedSample now that SelectionContext exists.
evidence: Playground.tsx:423-483 passes 49 individual props to PlaygroundContent despite 7 context providers wrapping it. PlaygroundContentProps (lines 496-546) enumerates all 49 members. MainCanvasProps in MainCanvas.tsx:79-142 has ~29 members (auditor's "32" is slightly overstated but directionally correct). The legacy comment is literal: line 286-287 reads `// Sample selection state for cross-chart highlighting (legacy - kept for backward compatibility)` with `const [selectedSample, setSelectedSample] = useState<number | null>(null)`, and these are drilled as props at lines 481-482 and typed at lines 544-545, while SelectionContext is already mounted at line 419.

title: SelectionContext value memoizes on the whole state object, defeating granular re-render control even for action-only consumers
impact: Even toolbars/panels that never display sample data re-render on every click-to-select; the 'read-only for performance' hook is misleading because it does not subscribe to a narrower slice. Compounds FE-ARCH-03's cascade.
fix: Split the context into a stable SelectionActionsContext (callbacks only, memoized once) and the existing state/store path; have action-only consumers use the actions context. Make useSelectionState() route through the useSyncExternalStore selector store rather than useSelection().

impact: Anyone following scripts/build.py (referenced by docs and the orphan NSIS installer) gets a hard build failure. The dual specs make it ambiguous which packaging model is real, guaranteeing wasted effort and broken release attempts.
fix: Pick the Electron model (backend.spec) as the single source of truth. Delete nirs4all-studio.spec, scripts/build.py, and scripts/build.sh (the pywebview monolith path) since launcher.py/pywebview were removed. Keep only build-backend.cjs + build-release.cjs + electron-builder.yml. Update docs/PACKAGING.md / ELECTRON.md accordingly.
evidence: All four cited locations are confirmed accurate: `nirs4all-studio.spec:228` references `launcher.py` which does not exist; `scripts/build.py:156` sets `spec_file = project_dir / 'nirs4all-studio.spec'`; `backend.spec:188` uses `main.py` (which exists); `scripts/build-backend.cjs:143` invokes `PyInstaller backend.spec`. The pywebview-monolith model in `nirs4all-studio.spec` (gtk/cocoa/edgechromium imports at lines 104, 148–175) is entirely contradictory to the Electron+subprocess model used by `backend.spec`. However, `scripts/build.py` and `nirs4all-studio.spec` are not referenced by any CI workflow, npm script, or documentation file (`grep` across all .yml/.json/.md/.nsi returns zero hits). The broken path requires manual invocation of `python scripts/build.py`.

title: Custom Python self-updater targets a PyInstaller exe that the Electron build never produces
impact: The user-facing update feature is fundamentally mismatched to the package format: at best it no-ops, at worst it corrupts the install by overwriting Electron files with a backend-only staging dir. There is no working, safe update path for the desktop app.
fix: Decide the update model. For an Electron app, use electron-updater with electron-builder's publish provider (uncomment/configure electron-builder.yml:99) and drive updates from the main process, not from FastAPI. Remove updater/ + api/update_downloader.py self-update-by-cp logic, or scope it strictly to updating the in-venv nirs4all library (which venv_manager already handles) rather than the app binary.
evidence:
1. updater/__init__.py:72-79 — get_app_directory() uses sys.frozen/sys.executable (PyInstaller heuristic); lines 82-89 — get_executable_name() returns "nirs4all-studio.exe". The Windows/Unix script templates (lines 126-130, 187-196) do xcopy/cp -R over APP_DIR then relaunch EXECUTABLE.

2. electron-builder.yml:22 — asar: true confirmed; the real shipping artifacts are NSIS installer / DMG / AppImage. The app code lives in app.asar, not as loose files an external cp can replace. electron-builder.yml:99-103 — the publish block is commented out.

3. package.json — electron-updater is not a dependency; electron/ directory has no autoUpdater usage at all.

4. api/updates.py:990-1043 — the /webapp/apply POST endpoint is live and unconditional (no DESKTOP_MODE or sys.frozen guard), directly calling create_updater_script() + launch_updater(). The _find_platform_asset() helper (lines 528-566) matches .exe/.msi/.dmg/.AppImage/.deb — Electron installer packages, not staged directories a cp loop could apply.

5. In frozen/desktop mode, sys.executable points to the bundled PyInstaller backend inside extraResources/backend/, so APP_DIR would be that sub-directory — not the Electron app root — making the xcopy target wrong even structurally.

title: Standalone NSIS installer is orphaned, references missing icon and a PyInstaller layout that isn't built
impact: Two Windows installer paths, one broken; confusion over which to ship. The hand-written one cannot build (missing icon) and would install nothing meaningful.
fix: Delete installer/nsis/nirs4all-studio.nsi and rely on electron-builder's nsis target. If a custom NSIS script is genuinely needed, point electron-builder.nsis.script at it and fix the icon path to public/nirs4all.ico.
evidence: installer/nsis/nirs4all-studio.nsi:53-54 defines `!define MUI_ICON "..\..\public\icon.ico"` and `!define MUI_UNICON "..\..\public\icon.ico"`, but `ls public/*.ico` shows only `nirs4all.ico` — `icon.ico` does not exist. Line 103 uses `File /r "..\..\dist\nirs4all-studio\*.*"` which references a PyInstaller COLLECT directory never produced by the build pipeline. electron-builder.yml:35-44 already defines a working `nsis:` block using the correct `public/nirs4all.ico` path, confirming the hand-written script is a redundant duplicate.

title: No manual chunking / code-splitting: three.js + drei + fiber + regl + recharts all land in one bundle
impact: Large initial JS payload and slow first load, especially painful in the web deployment; Rollup will emit '>500kB chunk' warnings the build currently ignores. Heavy libs cannot be cached independently across releases.
fix: Add manualChunks to split vendor groups (three/@react-three/drei -> 'three', recharts -> 'charts', regl -> 'regl', radix/@radix-ui -> 'ui') in vite.config.ts build.rollupOptions.output, and lazy-load the heavy 3D/SHAP/synthesis pages with React.lazy + Suspense in App.tsx. Set a sane chunkSizeWarningLimit and treat warnings as signal.
evidence: vite.config.ts:117-120 confirms the build block contains only `outDir: "dist"` and `sourcemap` — no `rollupOptions`, no `manualChunks`, no `chunkSizeWarningLimit`. src/App.tsx:1-20 shows all 17 page components (Dashboard, Playground, PipelineEditor, SpectraSynthesis, VariableImportance, etc.) are statically imported with zero `React.lazy`/`import()`. package.json includes `"three": "^0.182.0"`, `"@react-three/drei": "^10.7.7"`, `"@react-three/fiber": "^9.5.0"`, `"regl": "^2.1.1"`, `"recharts": "2.15.4"` — all very large. Grep across `src/` finds 19 files importing these libs and zero `React.lazy` or dynamic `import()` at route level (one single dynamic import exists in `src/hooks/usePlaygroundQuery.ts:309` for an API helper, not a UI chunk).

title: Requirements files are floor-only (>=) with no upper bounds, no hashes, and no Python lockfile
impact: Non-reproducible backend builds; a green build today can become a broken bundle tomorrow from an upstream minor release, with no way to reconstruct the exact set that worked. Supply-chain integrity (hashes) is absent.
fix: Adopt a lockfile: pip-compile (pip-tools) or uv to produce a hash-pinned requirements lock per flavor (cpu/gpu/gpu-macos), and have build-backend.cjs install from the lock, not the floor file. Keep the loose .txt as the human-edited input only.
evidence: All five requirements files (`requirements.txt`, `requirements-cpu.txt`, `requirements-gpu.txt`, `requirements-gpu-macos.txt`, `requirements-test.txt`) use only `>=` floor pins — e.g., `requirements.txt:4` has `fastapi>=0.115.0`, line 5 `uvicorn[standard]>=0.34.0`, line 10 `pyinstaller>=6.12.0`. `grep '==' requirements*.txt` returns zero matches. No lockfile exists (`*.lock`, `uv.lock` absent). Two PyInstaller spec files (`backend.spec`, `nirs4all-studio.spec`) confirm the bundling context where version sensitivity is highest.

title: version.json is the runtime source of truth but is decoupled from package.json and only stamped by the dead build path
impact: Shipped builds report a hardcoded 1.0.0 / commit=development regardless of the actual release tag, making the update-available comparison and any telemetry/version reporting unreliable.
fix: Stamp version.json from the working pipeline: add a step in scripts/build-release.cjs (or a prebuild hook) that writes version.json from package.json version + git short SHA + UTC date, mirroring scripts/build.py:update_version_json. Or drop version.json and have get_webapp_version read package.json (the electron-builder source of truth).
evidence: The finding is substantiated but partially mitigated. `api/updates.py:387-415` (`get_webapp_version`) reads `version.json` first and only falls back to `package.json` if `version.json` is absent. `version.json` is committed as `{"version":"1.0.0","build_date":"2025-01-07T00:00:00Z","commit":"development"}` (version.json:1-5). The `electron-release.yml` workflow (which triggers on `v*` tags and builds Electron AppImage/deb via electron-builder) updates `package.json` with `npm version $VERSION` (electron-release.yml:131) but never stamps `version.json`, so it ships the stale committed file. By contrast, `release.yml` (the PyInstaller path) does correctly stamp `version.json` at prepare:73-82 and uploads it as an artifact to be picked up by each build job. The net effect is that Electron builds via `electron-release.yml` will report version `1.0.0` / commit `development` at runtime regardless of actual release tag, since the stale `version.json` is found before the fallback to the correctly-updated `package.json` is reached.

title: backend.spec keeps console=True — Windows Electron-spawned backend flashes a console window
impact: A stray black console window appears alongside the desktop app on Windows — looks broken/unprofessional and confuses users (closing it kills the backend).
fix: Set console=False for the bundled backend (logging is already captured via piped stdio in backend-manager.ts), or use a windowed bootloader and rely on the existing stdout/stderr pipes. If console output is needed for debugging, gate it behind an env flag rather than defaulting on.
evidence: backend.spec:223 — `console=True,  # Keep console for logging` in the EXE() call. electron/backend-manager.ts:197-201 — `spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], detached: false })` with stdout/stderr captured via .on('data') at lines 205-211. The console window is not needed for log capture since pipes already handle it.

title: GPU/Metal requirements are mostly comments — flavor builds install no GPU stack
impact: build:backend:gpu / build:release:gpu produce a mislabeled artifact (renamed with -gpu suffix in build-release.cjs:179) that has no GPU support, and the TF hidden-import can break the freeze. Users selecting the GPU build get CPU behavior.
fix: Either make requirements-gpu.txt actually list the GPU deps (e.g. nirs4all[gpu] / tensorflow[and-cuda] pinned) so the flavor is real, or remove the gpu/gpu-metal flavors entirely and document that GPU support is installed at runtime via venv_manager into the managed nirs4all venv (consistent with backend.spec excluding tensorflow at line 167-177).
evidence: requirements-gpu.txt (all lines): contains only `-r requirements-cpu.txt` plus 15 lines of comments (lines 7-22); zero actual GPU packages are installed for Linux/Windows CUDA builds. backend.spec:139-146 confirms IS_GPU_BUILD adds tensorflow/keras hidden-imports, and backend.spec:167-177 confirms the CPU path explicitly excludes tensorflow — meaning the GPU path is expected to supply it but requirements-gpu.txt provides nothing. build-release.cjs:179-187 renames outputs with a `-gpu` suffix anyway. The macOS case (requirements-gpu-macos.txt:9-10) does install tensorflow-macos and tensorflow-metal, but nirs4all[macos-gpu] is still commented out (lines 17-18). The hidden-import mismatch for the CUDA flavor will cause PyInstaller warnings or failures when tensorflow is absent.

title: Icon assets are inconsistent across builders; macOS uses a PNG where .icns is required and the PyInstaller spec points at files that don't exist
impact: Inconsistent/broken app iconography per platform; macOS build likely ships a wrong or low-quality icon; any path that touches nirs4all-studio.spec or the NSIS icon fails. Cross-platform branding is unreliable.
fix: Generate a proper icon set (nirs4all.icns for mac, nirs4all.ico for win, 512px png for linux) and reference consistent names: electron-builder mac/linux -> the .icns/512px png; win -> public/nirs4all.ico. Remove the stale spec/NSIS icon refs together with the dead specs.
evidence: electron-builder.yml:56 `icon: public/nirs4all_logo.png` (mac) and :80 `icon: public/nirs4all_logo.png` (linux) — confirmed, a PNG is used instead of .icns for macOS. nirs4all-studio.spec:290-296: references `nirs4all_icon.ico` and `nirs4all_icon.icns`, both confirmed missing from `public/`; however the spec guards these with `if ico_path.exists()` so PyInstaller simply builds without an icon rather than failing. installer/nsis/nirs4all-studio.nsi:53-54: `!define MUI_ICON "..\..\public\icon.ico"` — `public/icon.ico` confirmed missing; this NSIS script will fail to compile if invoked. Only `public/nirs4all.ico` exists (referenced correctly in electron-builder.yml win block at :32).

title: Launcher stop/clean uses broad pkill -f patterns that can kill unrelated user processes
impact: Running `npm run stop`/`clean`/`restart` (which calls cmd_stop) can terminate the user's editor, other Electron apps, and unrelated dev servers — data loss and severe surprise on a shared/dev machine, especially on WSL/Linux where 'electron' matches many GUI apps.
fix: Kill by the saved PIDs from $PID_DIR/*.pid (and their process groups) instead of broad pkill -f. Scope any name match to a unique marker (e.g. cwd-specific or a custom argv tag) and never pattern-kill 'electron'/'vite' globally.
evidence: scripts/launcher.sh lines 164-168: `pkill -f "vite"`, `pkill -f "python main.py"`, `pkill -f "electron"`, `pkill -f "esbuild"` — all broad pattern kills with no scope. The `save_pid`/`get_pid` infrastructure exists (lines 94-110, PID files written at lines 243, 251, 294) but `cmd_stop()` never calls `get_pid` — it only clears PIDs at line 185 after the pattern-kill. The `pkill -f "electron"` pattern will match any Electron-based app (VS Code, Slack, etc.) running on the machine.

title: Frontend bundle sourcemaps are emitted and uploaded only conditionally; default prod build ships no maps and Sentry stack traces are unsymbolicated
impact: Crash reports from production builds are effectively unreadable unless the release pipeline always sets the full Sentry env triple — easy to forget, silently degrading observability that the project clearly invested in (Sentry deps + telemetry modules).
fix: Always emit hidden sourcemaps for prod (sourcemap: 'hidden') and make Sentry upload a hard requirement of the release job (fail the build if Sentry env is missing during a tagged release), so symbolication is guaranteed and maps are never shipped to users.
evidence: vite.config.ts:13-17 defines `shouldUploadSentrySourceMaps = Boolean(SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN && SENTRY_ORG && SENTRY_PROJECT)`. vite.config.ts:119 sets `sourcemap: mode === "development" || shouldUploadSentrySourceMaps` — no sourcemaps in a normal production build without the env triple. vite.config.ts:96-110 conditionally activates the Sentry plugin with `filesToDeleteAfterUpload: ["dist/**/*.map", "dist-electron/**/*.map"]` only when the triple is present. electron-builder.yml:12 contains `"!**/*.map"` under `files:`, stripping any remaining maps from the packaged Electron app. package.json lines 101-102 confirm `@sentry/electron` and `@sentry/react` are runtime deps, confirming the project actively uses Sentry for crash reporting.

title: Node engine constraint disagrees with .nvmrc and CLAUDE.md (>=20 vs pinned 22)
impact: Mild but real: builds can pass on an unintended Node version, and the loose floor undermines the explicit Node-22 pin the rest of the repo relies on.
fix: Tighten engines.node to '>=22' (or '^22') to match .nvmrc, and consider engine-strict=true in .npmrc so the constraint is enforced rather than advisory.
evidence: package.json:9-11 declares `"node": ">=20"`, while .nvmrc:1 pins `22`. The cited ensure-linux-node.cjs does NOT enforce Node version — it only blocks Windows Node running against WSL paths (lines 10-31), making no version check at all. The engines floor mismatch is real and unmitigated by any runtime gate.
